issues.description: Regression gate failed (regressions_ran=3, regressions_passed=false; run_status=rejected). The production hunk is semantically equivalent to upstream, so the most likely culprit is the patch's own added Spock specs in ClasspathResourceSpec.groovy: they assume symbols (`PATH`, `SAME_FOLDER_RESOURCE_CONTENT`, `content()`) and an exception contract (`IllegalStateException` with message containing "would go above root") that are not evidenced in the diff context, and the `"..\\util\\same-folder.txt"` case additionally assumes a fixture resource exists. A Groovy compile error in the spec class fails the whole suite. Must be verified/fixed before acceptance.

Divergence from upstream mechanism: `split("[/\\]+")` compiles a Pattern on every forFile() call and collapses separator runs, whereas the official `replace('\\','/')` + `split("/")` is cheaper and keeps the pre-existing "sequential slashes" empty-term path exercised. No behavioral difference (empty terms are skipped), but it makes future merges with upstream noisier.

Cosmetic: with our patch the "would go above root" IllegalStateException message echoes the original backslash-containing relativePath, while the official fix reports the normalized forward-slash form. Any test or log matcher keyed to the normalized form would differ.
Test hygiene: the `where:` block declares an unused `description` column and four largely redundant traversal cases; the `BS` constant indirection adds little over a plain escaped literal.

result.root_cause: AbstractResource.forFile canonicalized and root-checked the relative path by splitting only on '/', so a backslash-delimited \"..\" segment survived as an opaque term, passed the above-root guard, and was later re-interpreted as a directory separator by the downstream container/filesystem, escaping the resource root.
result.summary: Our patch fixes the real root cause at the same chokepoint as the official fix: it makes AbstractResource.forFile treat '\' as a path separator before term-splitting, so backslash traversal segments become genuine ".." terms and hit the pre-existing pop/above-root boundary check. The mechanism differs cosmetically (regex `split("[/\\]+")` vs upstream's `replace('\\','/')` + `split("/")`) but is semantically equivalent, since empty terms are already skipped by the loop, and the POV no longer reproduces. The blocking problem is not the security logic but the patch's own test additions: the regression suite fails (3 ran, none passing) and the run was rejected, most plausibly because the new ClasspathResourceSpec cases reference unverified fixtures/constants and assume an exception type and message not evidenced here. Fix or drop those specs and this becomes an accept-quality fix.
